content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am using an [product_name] HMI [article_no] together with a [product_name] relay. Both devices are connected via Ethernet using TCP/IP. I now want to connect the HMI to our [company_name] computer network in order to save some process data to the server. These data are analog values wired to the relay. Is this possible, and what would the required steps be regarding IP settings? (The HMI has one Ethernet interface and two ports.) Thank you.
The HMI and the relay should be on the same IP subnet as your [company_name] network.

analysis.insight_summary: The user wants to add an HMI and relay device to a company network to save process data on a server but is unsure about IP configuration and how practical this setup is. The primary usability issue is the lack of clear, step-by-step instructions for networking these devices with existing company infrastructure to enable reliable data transfer.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects easy-to-follow networking steps for integrating HMI and relay devices into a company network for routine data storage. They assume data can be transferred and stored on the server with minimal configuration complexity.
